notes: Read all three units, full civil-liberties context, all nine candidates and the review. Restored U.S. scope to constitutional institutions and federal intelligence and law-enforcement agencies; contextualized the incumbent as the then-current U.S. administration without guessing a name; preserved its claimed freedom-spreading purpose; identified the U.S. Supreme Court; retained Guantanamo's worst-abuses comparison; and attached the predicted attention shift to the entire preceding package of changes. Also restored the omitted commitment to leadership reflecting Americans' decency and aspirations.

claims.claim_text: Belief that the U.S. Constitution, courts, institutions and traditions work.

Although claiming to spread freedom worldwide, the then-current U.S. administration's overseas operations tragically helped create potential adversaries threatening to make the United States less secure.
Commitment to give U.S. intelligence and law-enforcement agencies tools to hunt down and take out terrorists without undermining the U.S. Constitution, freedom or privacy.
Commitment to lead toward a freer and safer world in ways reflecting the American people's decency and aspirations.
Commitment to respect habeas corpus, the centuries-old right to challenge one's detention terms that the U.S. Supreme Court had recently reaffirmed.
Commitment to close the Guantanamo Bay detention camp, described as the location of many of the preceding years' worst constitutional abuses.

The proposed package ending rendition to torture, detention without trial or charge, secret prisons and Guantanamo detention while respecting habeas corpus would redirect world attention to terrorists' actions against the United States rather than U.S. treatment of suspects.
